rulings.evidence: Tenderized round steak sold on its own tray by the pound; board reports ABSENT (no commodity, no capture), so a new id is proposed. 4 x 1/3 lb = 604 g raw.
buttermilk is a live board id priced 5/7 - a reuse the vocabulary simply has no name row for. Full 490 g is stated because the whole quart is bought even though the soak is drained.
"Large" is the grade the `eggs` id already prices; 50 g per shelled large egg.
Plain dredging flour is the vocabulary's All-Purpose Flour; 1 cup scooped and levelled is 125 g.
Two-word spelling of the existing Cornstarch row and the `cornstarch` id priced 7/7 - a reuse, not a new food. 1 cup is 128 g.

A Lawry's-style seasoning blend at spice-aisle prices, not the salt canister; mapping it to `salt` would publish a wrong price. The estate already prices celery-salt as its own id, so the precedent is for splitting.
Same food as the dredge line, here as the gravy roux; 1 tbsp is 7.8 g.
The fat left in the skillet after frying the steaks - it is already bought as the vegetable oil line, so it carries no id and no weight of its own rather than double-counting.
fresh-thyme is a live board id (4/7); no bridge to dried-thyme, which is a different price and weight. One sprig is about 1 g.
Second occurrence of the same blend, in the gravy.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Mechanically tenderized round steak, sold on a tray by the pound in the fresh beef case. Board reports ABSENT: no commodity, no capture match. Checked by food across the namespaces: the beef ids in play are ground (ground-beef-8020) and roasts; cube steak is neither, it is a thin tenderized steak at its own price per lb, and no word-order variant (cubed steak / minute steak / tenderized round steak) is carried. This is the recipe's main protein, so a null here would leave the dish uncostable.

A blended seasoning (salt, paprika, turmeric, garlic, onion) sold as an 8 oz spice-aisle bottle at several dollars, against a 26 oz salt canister at well under one. Mapping it to `salt` would be a price-class stretch of an order of magnitude. The estate already treats blended and flavoured salts as their own ids (celery-salt), and no existing id (salt, garlic-powder, paprika) covers the blend under another spelling.
